traceability.evidence: Rule implementation exists for this story: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts, with JSDoc linking it directly to docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md and all listed REQ-TEST-* requirement IDs.,Helper logic is implemented in src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts, covering: - REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT via determineIsTestFile (substring-based test-file detection using directories and .test./.spec. markers) - REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS and REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID via ensureFileSupportsAnnotation (enforces presence of @supports; deeper validation is delegated to existing valid-story-reference and valid-req-reference rules from dependent stories 006.0 and 010.0) - REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT via isTestCallName handling describe, it, test, context (Jest/Mocha/Jasmine-style) and MemberExpression forms like describe.each/test.only - REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX and auto-fix behavior via normalizeReqPrefixInDescription and handleItOrTestCall - REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT via handleCallExpression + handleDescribeCall, which enforce describe-pattern matching on all describe() calls in test files.,Rule metadata and behavior in src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts match the story’s acceptance criteria: - File-level annotations: create() calls ensureFileSupportsAnnotation for any file recognized as a test file; meta.messages.missingFileSupports = "Test file must have @supports annotation listing tested requirements." (AC: File-Level Annotations) - Describe block story references: handleCallExpression creates a CallExpression visitor that, for calleeName === 'describe', checks the first argument against describeRegex (default "Story [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+-") and reports messageId "missingDescribeStory" when it doesn’t match (AC: Describe Block Story References). - Test-name requirement prefixes: for 'it' and 'test', handleItOrTestCall enforces names starting with /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/, reporting messageId "missingReqPrefix" and optionally normalizing malformed prefixes (AC: Test Name Requirement Prefixes). - Quality/ESLint best practices: meta.type = "problem", meta.schema fully validates options (testFilePatterns, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, describePattern, autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, testSupportsTemplate) with additionalProperties: false; fixable: "code" is used only for safe text transformations (inserting comment template, normalizing existing REQ prefixes). Implementation uses context.getFilename, context.getSourceCode, and standard visitor patterns (AC: Quality Standards). - Integration: src/index.ts includes "require-test-traceability" in RULE_NAMES and maps "traceability/require-test-traceability" to "error" in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, and both recommended and strict presets include that map, so the rule is fully wired into the plugin and flat-config presets (AC: Integration).,Dedicated tests for this story and its companion auto-fix story exist and pass: - tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts is explicitly annotated with: * @supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT * @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md ... - Jest output (npm test -- --runInBand --verbose) shows this suite passing under the description: "require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0)" with both valid and invalid cases: * Valid cases: - File with file-level @supports and correct describe + it('[REQ-EXAMPLE] ...') (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS) - Mocha-style context('Story 020.0-...', ...) demonstrating framework compatibility (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT) - A non-test file filename (src/not-a-test-file.ts) is ignored even with describe present (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT) - A test with already-correct [REQ-TRACE-123] prefix remains unchanged under auto-fix (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT) * Invalid cases with expected errors and, where applicable, auto-fix output: - Missing @supports in a test file yields messageId "missingFileSupports" and inserts a placeholder @supports block at the top matching the story’s example template (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - A describe without any story reference ("no story reference here") triggers messageId "missingDescribeStory" (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY). - it('missing prefix', ...) triggers messageId "missingReqPrefix" with no auto-fix (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - Malformed prefixes '[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]', '[REQ_TEST_FIX]', '[req-lowercase]', and '(REQ-PAREN)' are all auto-fixed to canonical '[REQ-TEST-FIX]' or '[REQ-LOWERCASE]' / '[REQ-PAREN]' by normalizeReqPrefixInDescription, with messageId "missingReqPrefix" (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE).,Existing deep-validation and file-validation rules (dependencies from stories 005.0, 006.0, 010.0, 010.2) already enforce that @supports paths and requirement IDs are valid, and they run on all files, including tests: - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts validates story path existence, extension, path traversal security, absolute path restrictions, and configuration for storyDirectories and allowAbsolutePaths. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts validates that referenced requirement IDs exist in story files, including multi-story @supports lines. Thus REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID is satisfied by composition: require-test-traceability ensures presence of @supports in test files; valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, and valid-req-reference (from dependency stories) ensure those annotations are well-formed and point to real stories/requirements.,Documentation for the rule exists and matches the story’s design: - README.md lists `traceability/require-test-traceability` with a one-line description exactly aligned with this story (file-level @supports, story references in describe, and [REQ-...] in it/test names). - user-docs/api-reference.md has a full section "traceability/require-test-traceability" (lines ~198–255) documenting: * Behavior: file-level @supports, top-level describe story references, [REQ-XXX] prefixes in it/test names. * All configuration options requested in the story: testFilePatterns, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, describePattern, autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, testSupportsTemplate. * Default severity = error and that the rule is enabled in both recommended and strict presets. * Example code block demonstrating the intended usage (file-level @supports, describe with story reference, tests with [REQ-...] names). This satisfies the "Documentation" acceptance criterion and the Definition of Done item for documentation.,Plugin integration and presets confirm the rule is part of the standard configuration and behaves as specified: - src/index.ts includes "require-test-traceability" in RULE_NAMES and dynamically requires ./rules/require-test-traceability. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/require-test-traceability" to "error" and is used to build both recommended and strict flat-config presets, satisfying "Rule added to recommended configuration" and making the rule active by default in normal usage. - Jest test output confirms flat-config presets integration works (tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts) and that the recommended/strict presets include all core rules; that suite passes successfully.,All project tests, including those for this story, pass: - Command used: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Result: 39 test suites passed, 299 tests passed total, including the suite "require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0)" and all its valid/invalid scenarios. This demonstrates the behavior of require-test-traceability is verified end-to-end and functions correctly within the plugin’s test infrastructure.
traceability.notes: The story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION is fully implemented. The ESLint rule traceability/require-test-traceability and its helpers enforce file-level @supports annotations in test files, require story references in describe() strings via a configurable describePattern, and enforce [REQ-XXX] prefixes in it()/test() names with safe normalization auto-fixes for malformed prefixes. Test-file detection is configurable and defaults match typical Jest/Mocha layouts and naming. Framework compatibility is achieved by recognizing describe, it, test, and context as test-call names and also handling MemberExpression forms like describe.each/test.only. The deeper validation of @supports paths and requirement IDs is delegated to existing rules from dependency stories (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference), as intended. Comprehensive RuleTester coverage plus passing Jest output, along with detailed user documentation and plugin configuration wiring, collectively satisfy all acceptance criteria and Definition-of-Done items for this story.
